questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to find university in an English-speaking country, with courses that matched my interests.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would give a higher rating if it wasn't for the Covid restrictions on in-person teaching.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy except for the fact that the abundance of information could make it difficult to find exactly what I was looking for.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was sent some very helpful guides and reminders via email, and in any case, I knew that I could reach out to the visiting student office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I know that several welcome events took place during the first weeks, but I did not participate.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed with some friends of my family, so I wouldn't know.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I looked into private student housing, and had trouble finding any that was available for one semester only. I think your best bet would probably be to team up with other exchange students and find a flat to share.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university's on-campus housing is guaranteed for every student, except those who will only stay for one semester. You can be placed on a waiting list, but I wouldn't count on finding a room this way.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There's a pretty straight-forward online survey, that guides you through dropping or adding courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always email the visiting student office, it might just take a few days to get a response.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed my courses a few times, because I was hoping for a spot to open up on a specific course that I wanted, which unfortunately didn't happen. In the end, I had to make a change at the very last minute, and had to choose a course that I didn't really want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's not a lot of spaces for exchange students on most courses, but I would recommend contacting the course organizers, as some will have a waiting list.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took happened to be intended for 1st or 2nd year students, which meant that they weren't too challenging - they weren't easy either, but I didn't feel out of depths.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar - we had weekly online lectures, and would then discuss the material in small tutorial groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding Gender in the Contemporary World
Introduction to Social Anthropology
Scottish Literature 2a

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There's a few courses on Scotland, and Scottish literature and culture, which are aimed specifically at exchange students - might be a good place to meet people as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to book a Covid test to take after arrival, which was 68 pounds.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cafes, coffee shops etc were cheaper than I expected, especially the ones around campus. I also saved some money by getting most of my course materials from the university library.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's hundreds of societies to choose from, there'll be something for anyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't actually join any, so I wouldn't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you get the chance to travel around Scotland, I recommend taking the train up to Inverness and going from there - there's plenty of bus tours available which take you around to see the most beautiful sights.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I don't think Scottish culture is all that different from Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would think that societies are the best place to meet like-minded people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing except for how overly polite some people are, it almost made me uncomfortable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Again, people are very polite, and most of time it's really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Use the campus! The library is a great place to study, and the student association has several amazing cafes, bars etc. 2. Reach out and connect with your teachers and lecturers - they're always really cool about it. 3. Don't just stay in the most central areas of the city. I recommend taking a walk around Stockbridge, Morningside or Leith.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is really committed to ending period poverty, so you can get free period products anywhere on campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I felt so so privileged to be taught at such a prestigious institution and it definitely boosted my confidence in my own academic capabilities that I was able to do well in my courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There's an overwhelming amount of information, deadlines and documents to keep track off, so you really need to stay organized and keep a detailed diary.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
